runtime_proof.note: Increment 3. Two production startup defects on one activation path. The worker defect was reproduced by a failed production promote and repaired; the Command Center defect was reproduced against the running production container and is proven repaired by an image built at this head and started on exactly the key set deploy.yml writes. The canonical deploy was NOT run -- dispatching a production deployment is reserved -- so the image-level start is the honest stand-in, and it is labelled as one.

queries.name: the official-picks kill switch is explicitly engaged
queries.method: read-only SELECT against production zfzdnfwdarxucxtaojxm: `select target, killed, updated_at from delivery_kill_switch where target in ('official-picks','best-bets','trader-insights','exclusive-insights')`
queries.result: 4 rows, all killed=true. official-picks killed=true, updated_at 2026-09-17 21:24:35.602039+00.
queries.significance: Increment 1 relied on the ABSENCE of the row (isKilled returns true for an unknown target). PM added an explicit engaged row, so the prepared state no longer rests on a default. Read back 10 consecutive times across both deploy attempts and the rollback; true every time.

queries.name: no official-picks delivery was ever enqueued
queries.method: read-only SELECT: `select count(*) from distribution_outbox where target = 'discord:official-picks'`
queries.significance: The worker crash-looped in createWorkerRuntimeDependencies, before any delivery path was constructed. This confirms mechanically that the failure could not have delivered, rather than inferring it from the stack trace.

queries.name: the pre-existing outbox was untouched by the attempt
queries.method: read-only SELECT: `select count(*), max(created_at) from distribution_outbox`
queries.result: 5747 rows, newest 2026-07-30 20:04:41.893448+00 — identical before Phase A, after Phase A, after the Phase B failure and after the rollback
queries.significance: Turning the worker on is inert against the 5,747 legacy rows: the claim loop and the stale-claim reaper are both target-scoped, and automated recovery is disabled. An unchanged newest-row timestamp is the measurement of that, not a claim about it.

queries.name: nothing was delivered on the day of the attempt
queries.method: read-only SELECT: `select count(*) from distribution_outbox where status = 'sent' and created_at >= current_date`
queries.significance: Covers the whole window containing both deploy attempts and the rollback.

queries.name: the governed pick cohort is intact and Track Only
queries.method: read-only SELECT: `select count(*) from picks where metadata ? 'distributionMode'`
queries.result: 6 — the 4 pre-existing plus the 2 submitted through the deployed Smart Form at 21:45:31Z and 21:47:00Z, both capper_id=griff843, both distributionMode=track-only, both carrying deliveryAuthorization.decision='refused' with reason 'human-delivery-posture-off'
queries.significance: The human-capper authorization path from increment 1 is running in production and refusing per pick, recorded on the row rather than inferred.

queries.name: the running worker container's posture after rollback
queries.method: docker exec unit-talk-worker-1 printenv, read from the running production container
queries.significance: Parked posture restored, read from the process environment rather than from deploy logs. The distribution target is a raw channel id matching ^discord:\d+$, which is the escape hatch that lets parked mode start and human-capper mode does not have — the defect this increment fixes.
